title: What agile is, and why a framework alone is not enough
blurb: Define agile the way PRINCE2 Agile does, and explain why adopting a framework does not guarantee its benefits.
question: An organization has bought a backlog tool and renamed its meetings 'sprints', but delivery is no faster. According to PRINCE2 Agile, what has it misunderstood about agile?

teach.h: Agile is a way of thinking and working
teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile describes agile as a way of thinking and working that favours adaptation, collaboration and experimentation. Teams learn from feedback and pivot quickly, which helps them reduce waste and delay and deliver solutions shaped around users. In plain English: try something small, see how users respond, learn, and change course early rather than late.

The book warns against assuming that adopting a framework guarantees benefits such as faster delivery or higher-quality products. A framework gives structure, but agile's real value comes from a shift in mindset. That needs a culture that lets teams self-manage, make decisions themselves and drive innovation. Agile is less about rigid adherence to a framework and more about collaboration, creativity and adaptability.

teach.h: Framework only, or framework plus mindset

teach.body: If people are not given the freedom to think and act in an agile way, calling processes, frameworks or techniques 'agile' means very little. The book calls this gap the difference between being agile and doing agile. Doing agile is using the frameworks, processes and terminology. Being agile is thinking that way and being allowed to apply it within agreed levels of self-management.

teach.h: How agile stays in name only

teach.body: Fernhill Housing Association adopts Scrum for its repairs-booking app. Six months on, nothing has improved: every backlog change still needs a senior manager's signature. Digital lead Tomasz Wojcik agrees decision boundaries with the board, then lets the team reorder its own backlog within them. Tenant feedback now changes the next iteration, and the most-requested feature ships within a month.

teach.text: Adopting Scrum, Kanban or a tool does not by itself deliver faster or better results. Agile's value lies in the shift in mindset and a culture that empowers teams. 'Being vs doing agile' is the name for the gap between the two.

items: Agile: a way of thinking and working that favours adaptation, collaboration, experimentation and learning from feedback.
Its aim: minimize waste and delays and deliver solutions focused on users.
Misconception: adopting a framework guarantees faster delivery or higher quality.
Real value comes from the mindset and a culture that lets teams self-manage and decide.

summary: You can now define agile as PRINCE2 Agile does: a way of thinking and working built on adaptation, collaboration, experimentation and feedback. You can also explain why a framework without the mindset and the freedom to use it does not guarantee the benefits.

A.q: Which statement best describes agile, as defined in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: A set of software tools for tracking team tasks
A way of thinking and working that favours adaptation
A delivery method that completes each phase in turn
A governance structure that replaces the project board
A.why: The book describes agile as a way of thinking and working favouring adaptation, collaboration, experimentation and learning from feedback (2.3).

whyNot.0: Tools can support agile, but agile is a way of thinking and working, not a toolset.
whyNot.2: Completing each phase before the next describes waterfall.
whyNot.3: Agile is not a governance structure; PRINCE2 Agile keeps the project board.

A.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, which statement is a common misconception about agile?
options: Teams should be empowered to manage themselves
Learning from feedback helps reduce waste
Agile ways of working favour collaboration
Adopting a framework guarantees the benefits
A.why: The book names, as a common misconception, the assumption that simply adopting a framework guarantees benefits such as faster delivery or higher quality (2.3).

whyNot.0: This is correct agile thinking: the book says teams should be empowered to self-manage.
whyNot.1: This is correct: feedback and quick pivots help agile teams minimize waste.
whyNot.2: This is correct: collaboration is central to agile.

A.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, where does the true value of agile lie?
A.why: The book says agile's true value lies in shifting mindsets, supported by a culture that empowers teams to self-manage and decide (2.3).

whyNot.1: Choosing a framework is the misconception the book warns about; a framework alone guarantees nothing.
whyNot.2: Detailed up-front planning is a feature of linear, waterfall delivery.
whyNot.3: Software may help, but it does not create the mindset that gives agile its value.

B.q: An organization renames its processes as agile, but staff still need approval for every decision. What does PRINCE2 Agile call this gap?
B.why: Labelling processes agile while people cannot think and act in an agile way is the gap between being and doing agile (2.3, 2.3.1).

whyNot.0: Waterfall versus agile contrasts two delivery approaches, not mindset and practice.
whyNot.1: Scaling concerns using agile across multiple teams and products.
whyNot.3: Values and principles are layers of the Agile Onion, not the name of this gap.

B.q: By experimenting, learning from feedback and pivoting quickly, what do agile teams aim to achieve?
B.why: The book links experimentation, feedback and quick pivots to minimizing waste, reducing delays and delivering user-focused solutions (2.3).

whyNot.1: Fixing all scope at the start works against adapting to feedback.
whyNot.2: Agile favours short cycles with frequent review, not long phases.
whyNot.3: Extra documentation is not the aim of agile ways of working.

B.q: What kind of culture does PRINCE2 Agile say an organization needs to gain real value from agile?
options: One where managers approve each task first
One that follows its chosen framework rigidly
One that fixes requirements very early
One that lets teams self-manage and decide
B.why: The book says organizations must embrace a culture that empowers teams to self-manage, make decisions independently and drive innovation (2.3).

whyNot.0: Approving each task removes the self-management agile depends on.
whyNot.1: The book says agile is less about rigid adherence to a framework.
whyNot.2: Fixing requirements early reduces the ability to adapt to feedback.

C.q:
Which two statements about agile are correct, according to PRINCE2 Agile?
1. Agile favours collaboration and learning from feedback.
2. Adopting Scrum guarantees higher-quality products.
3. Agile is mainly about strict adherence to one framework.
4. Calling processes agile means little if people cannot act in an agile way.
C.why: Agile favours collaboration and feedback (1), and labelling processes agile is meaningless without the freedom to be agile (4).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is the misconception the book warns about: no framework guarantees the benefits.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: a framework guarantees nothing, and agile is less about rigid adherence to one.
whyNot.3: Statement 3 is wrong: the book says agile is less about rigid adherence to a framework.

C.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. Agile teams reduce waste and delays by experimenting, learning from feedback and [?] quickly.
C.why: The book links experimentation, feedback and pivoting quickly to less waste and fewer delays (2.3).

whyNot.1: Escalating moves decisions upwards; it is not the agile behaviour described here.
whyNot.2: Documenting quickly is not what the definition stresses.
whyNot.3: Baselining fixes a version for control; it does not describe quick change of direction.

C.q: At Calder Freight, a team holds daily stand-ups and uses agile terms, but it keeps to the original plan even when users ask for changes. What is missing, and why does it matter?
options: A detailed plan, because agile needs more control
Another framework, because Scrum does not suit them
An agile mindset, because value comes from adapting
More stand-ups, because transparency drives change
C.why: The team is doing agile without being agile. Agile's value comes from the mindset of adapting to feedback, not from the rituals alone (2.3).

whyNot.0: A more detailed plan would make the team even less responsive to users.
whyNot.1: Changing framework is the misconception again: no framework guarantees benefits.
whyNot.3: More meetings add ritual, not the willingness to adapt that is missing.

reteach.title: A recipe is not cooking
reteach.question: Why does owning a framework not make a team agile?

blocks.body: A framework is like a recipe: it tells you the steps. Being agile is like being a cook who tastes as they go and adjusts. A team that follows the recipe but is not allowed to taste and adjust will turn out the same dish however the steps are labelled. PRINCE2 Agile wants teams that adapt, collaborate, experiment and learn from feedback, with the freedom to do so.

blocks.h: Will this change make us agile?

children.label: Being agile: where value comes from

blocks.text: If an option says a framework 'guarantees' faster delivery or better quality, it is the misconception PRINCE2 Agile warns about.

explain.body: Agile is a way of thinking and working that favours adaptation, collaboration, experimentation, learning from feedback and pivoting quickly (2.3).

test.q: Which group of ideas does PRINCE2 Agile use to describe agile?
test.why: Agile favours adaptation, collaboration, experimentation and learning from feedback (2.3).

whyNot.0: Prediction and sign-off fit a traditional, plan-driven approach.
whyNot.1: Sequential phases with handovers describe waterfall.
whyNot.2: Silos and approval chains are what agile tries to move away from.

explain.body: Simply adopting a framework does not guarantee benefits such as faster delivery or higher quality. The framework is structure; the value comes from the mindset (2.3).

test.q: A director says, 'Once we adopt Scrum, faster delivery is guaranteed.' How does PRINCE2 Agile view this?
options: As accurate, since Scrum is proven
As true once teams are trained
test.why: The book calls this a common misconception: adopting a framework does not guarantee benefits (2.3).

whyNot.0: No framework, however proven, guarantees the benefits without the mindset.
whyNot.2: The point applies to all projects, software included.
whyNot.3: Training helps, but the book's point is that the framework itself guarantees nothing.

explain.body: Agile's real value lies in shifting mindsets. That needs a culture that empowers teams to self-manage, make decisions and drive innovation (2.3).

explain.caption: Each level rests on the one below.

test.q: What does PRINCE2 Agile say organizations must embrace to get agile's true value?
test.why: The book says agile's value requires a culture that empowers teams to self-manage and make decisions (2.3).

whyNot.0: A strict hierarchy limits the self-management agile relies on.
whyNot.1: Choosing one framework is not where the value lies.
whyNot.3: Long up-front planning is typical of linear delivery.

explain.body: Doing agile is using the frameworks, processes and terms. Being agile is thinking that way and being allowed to act on it. Labels without the freedom to be agile mean little (2.3.1).

test.q: Which describes 'being agile' in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: Thinking in an agile way and being allowed to act on it
Using agile frameworks, processes and their terminology
Holding every agile event that the framework defines
Following an agile framework closely without changing it
test.why: Being agile is thinking in an agile way and being allowed to apply that mindset within appropriate self-management (2.3.1).

whyNot.2: Holding the events is part of doing agile.
whyNot.3: Rigid framework use is doing agile without being agile.
